Class Volumetric3DEffect

java.lang.Object
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.ConfigurableTextEffect
net.phoenix.chromatic_codes.api.effects.Volumetric3DEffect
All Implemented Interfaces:
IChromaticEffect
public class Volumetric3DEffect extends ConfigurableTextEffect
Adds offset background layers that make text look extruded.

Foreground and side colors are independent. The constructor's depth argument sets the layer count: positive values are truncated to an integer and nonpositive values use five. When configuring the effect, layers sets the number of background samples, while depth/angle or extensionX/extensionY set the total distance and direction. The renderer draws the farthest layers first, then the foreground.

Colors are packed RGB values; positions and offsets are in GUI pixels. Animated callbacks use the clock shared by the current draw and leave drawing to the renderer. Registrations share this object, so configure it before registering it and synchronize any later changes.

  • Constructor Details

    • Volumetric3DEffect

      public Volumetric3DEffect(float depth, List<Integer> colors)
      Creates the background layers used for extruded text.

      Use the movement factory to validate the palette, speeds and options: MovementRegistry.create. Direct construction skips that validation.

      Parameters:
      depth - legacy constructor layer count; positive values truncate to an integer, otherwise five is used
      colors - optional palette read once, not retained; missing front/side entries use white/#444444
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either of the palette entries read during construction is null

  • Method Details

    • isVolumetric

      public boolean isVolumetric()
      Advertises the extrusion capability; the native renderer also reads the layer geometry getters. Exposes the upstream volumetric capability flag.

      The 1.12 renderer obtains layer geometry from the concrete Volumetric3DEffect type. Returning true alone does not provide that geometry for an unrelated custom implementation.

      Returns:
      true to mark this effect as volumetric

    • getRenderColor

      public int getRenderColor(int c, float x, float y)
      Returns the primary foreground color; getSideColor supplies the extrusion layers. Chooses the color for the current glyph sample.

      The renderer can sample multiple corners to create a gradient. Return the input color when this effect should leave it unchanged. Supply transparency through IChromaticEffect.getOpacity(); alpha bits in the returned color are ignored.

      Parameters:
      c - incoming packed RGB; the foreground palette selects the result
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      packed RGB for this sample

    • getScale

      public float getScale(float x, float y)
      Keeps the glyph's size unchanged. Supplies one size multiplier for both axes.

      A value other than one takes precedence over separate axis scales in the native renderer. Use one here when IChromaticEffect.getScaleX(float, float) and IChromaticEffect.getScaleY(float, float) should control the shape independently.

      Parameters:
      x - horizontal sample position in GUI pixels
      y - vertical sample position in GUI pixels
      Returns:
      one
